reuse.why: Builds on recurConfigToRSchedule, getDateWithSkippedWeekend, RSchedule and dayFromDate throughout, and extends getDateWithSkippedWeekend for holidays rather than writing a second adjuster.

duplication.why: getDatesInRange re-creates getUpcomingDates' RSchedule construction, weekend-adjust map and breadcrumb handling, and the new RSchedule({ rrules, exdates }) pairing is spelled out at each construction site instead of in one builder.

placement.why: Recurrence rules and weekend/holiday adjustment live in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in schedules/app.ts, but the daily-frequency rule is decided in three places (recurConfigToRSchedule, recurConfigToExdates and getDatesInRange).

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps: daily skip, range handler, holidays and yearly holidays, with tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Two mechanisms for 'off days' (byDayOfWeek/exdates for daily vs. forward/backward stepping otherwise), exdates that every RSchedule caller must remember to pass, and a 200-year expansion of MM-DD holidays make the design fragile.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedules/app.ts getDatesInRange re-decides the daily exception with its own `config.frequency !== 'daily'` check instead of relying on recurConfigToRSchedule/getDateWithSkippedWeekend; find-schedules.ts takeDates still builds RSchedule without recurConfigToExdates.

disguised_duplication.where: getDatesInRange in schedules/app.ts reshapes getUpcomingDates' occurrence + skip-weekend pipeline (range bounds with a margin and a Set instead of take/count) rather than sharing it.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter; recurConfigToRSchedule gains a daily skipWeekend branch and the new recurConfigToExdates a daily-only branch with yearly expansion; getDatesInRange checks frequency !== 'daily' itself.
